bug_semantics: GET /api/invoices/{id} (App\API\InvoiceController::getAction) authorized only the role permission view_invoice. Symfony's ParamConverter loaded any Invoice by numeric id and the handler serialized it, with no CustomerVoter 'access' check on invoice.getCustomer(). ROLE_TEAMLEAD grants view_invoice, so a teamlead assigned only to Team B could read invoices for customers assigned exclusively to Team A (IDOR / CWE-285, CWE-862). The collection endpoint scoped results via InvoiceArchiveQuery::setCurrentUser() (later BaseApiController::prepareQuery), but the single-item path bypassed that query. The web downloadAction already required is_granted('access', subject.getCustomer()) on the invoice.
flaw_origin: The missing customer-scope check was first written when PR #5070 added src/API/InvoiceController.php. Member 0714fc6ac6576e83a035ca2f4090dd7a97ee8e93 created getAction with only #[IsGranted('view_invoice')] and returned the ParamConverter entity. At that same revision, sibling API get endpoints already used object-level voters (view on customer/project/activity/timesheet) and web InvoiceController::downloadAction already had #[IsGranted(new Expression("is_granted('access', subject.getCustomer())"), 'invoice')]. Original tests covered ROLE_USER denial and ROLE_ADMIN success, not cross-team customer isolation. The mechanism survived unchanged on main from squash 8de54e1fa7ffe3b911c93080f4abd0210bbc22b0 through 2.50.0 until 2.51.0 added the web-equivalent Expression.
